title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,infinity}. pi_{0,3} = pi_1(U_{0,3}) is free on two of the loops rho_0, rho_1, rho_infinity. The convention forced by the margin note is rho_infinity rho_1 rho_0 = 1, i.e. rho_0 = rho_1^{-1} rho_infinity^{-1}.

The groups involved.
- pi_{0,3}^tau: the extension of pi_{0,3} by complex conjugation tau. It is generated by three involutions tau_0, tau_1, tau_infinity, giving Z/2*Z/2*Z/2, the cartographic group of triangulated maps. Here rho_infinity = tau_1 tau_0, etc.
- pi_{0,3}^{D_3} = pi_1(U_{0,3}, S_3; P_+): the fundamental group of U_{0,3} with its operator group S_3, i.e. the orbifold/stack fundamental group of [U_{0,3}/S_3]. This is the j-line with orbifold points of order 2 and 3 and one cusp.
- pi_{0,3}^{D_3,tau}: the same with S_3 x {1,tau}.

The isomorphisms (40) from the previous page.
- pi_{0,3}^{D_3} is isomorphic to pi_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_infinity^3> = Z/2*Z/3.
- pi_{0,3}^{D_3,tau} is isomorphic to pi_{0,3}^tau/<rho_1^2, rho_infinity^3>, the extended (2,3,infinity) triangle reflection group.
- Combinatorially, these quotient groups classify maps whose faces are of order dividing 3 (monogons or triangles).

This page writes the isomorphisms out explicitly on generators.

(41), oriented case:
- rho (the order-3 symmetry) maps to rho_infinity^{-1}. The marginal remark 'Attention: l'exposant!' insists on the inverse.
- sigma_infinity (the involution) maps to rho_1.
- Hence epsilon_0 = sigma_infinity rho maps to rho_1 rho_infinity^{-1}, which equals rho_0 in the quotient because rho_1^2 = 1.

(42), unoriented case:
- tau_infinity maps to tau_infinity.
- tau_0 = rho(tau_infinity) maps to rho_infinity^{-1} tau_infinity rho_infinity.
- tau_1 = rho^2(tau_infinity) maps to rho_infinity^{-2} tau_infinity rho_infinity^2, which equals rho_infinity tau_infinity rho_infinity^{-1} because rho_infinity^3 = 1.
- The side computations re-express these in two ways: as words tau_0 tau_1 tau_infinity tau_1 tau_0 and tau_1 tau_0 tau_infinity tau_0 tau_1; and as (rho_infinity^{-1} rho_1 rho_infinity^{-1} rho_1) tau_infinity and (rho_infinity rho_1 rho_infinity rho_1) tau_infinity.
- These use the NB: tau_infinity acts on rho_infinity by tau_infinity(rho_infinity) = rho_0 rho_1 = rho_1^{-1} rho_infinity^{-1} rho_1 = rho_1 rho_infinity^{-1} rho_1.

The generators rho, sigma_i, epsilon_i are said to be defined in the standard way (apparently in §4), and tau_i are as in (24)/(21).

The modular identification. Replace U_{0,3} with its S_3 action by the Poincare half-plane Sigma^+ with the homographic action of SL(2,Z)/±1, resp. the homographic and anti-homographic action of GL(2,Z)/±1. Since Sigma^+ is simply connected, its fundamental group with operators is the operator group itself. This gives:
- (43) PGL(2,Z) isomorphic to pi_{0,3}^{D_3,tau}, isomorphic to pi_{0,3}^tau/<rho_1^2, rho_infinity^3>.
- (44) PSL(2,Z) isomorphic to pi_{0,3}^{D_3}, isomorphic to pi_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_infinity^3>.

Purpose. The page serves to give the 'remarkable elements' of the Teichmüller-type groupoid concrete matrix interpretations; this is done on the next page. It also prepares a generalization to Pi_{0,n} and regular n-gons via discrete subgroups of GL(2,R), which is announced but not carried out.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All the identities in (41)-(42) check out given the conventions rho_infinity rho_1 rho_0 = 1, rho_infinity = tau_1 tau_0 and tau_infinity(rho_infinity) = rho_1 rho_infinity^{-1} rho_1, using rho_1^2 = rho_infinity^3 = 1.

Minor point: epsilon_0 maps to rho_1 rho_infinity^{-1}. This equals rho_0 = rho_1^{-1} rho_infinity^{-1} only after imposing rho_1^2 = 1, so it holds in the quotient, not in pi_{0,3} itself. That is consistent with the statement.

ideas.what: Fundamental group of U_{0,3} with operator group S_3 (resp. S_3 x Z/2) relative to a base-point set P_+, identified with Z/2*Z/3 (resp. the extended (2,3,infinity) triangle group).
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold/stack fundamental group of [M_{0,4}/S_3], i.e. of M_{1,1}; equivariant fundamental groupoid (Brown's orbit groupoid)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Poincaré); orbifold version Thurston; groupoid version R. Brown, Higgins
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the S_3 action and the cartographic and modular groups, but not this explicit groupoid formalism

ideas.what: Quotients of cartographic groups by rho_1^2 and rho_infinity^3 classify maps with all faces of order dividing 3, and are isomorphic to PSL(2,Z) / PGL(2,Z).
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between trivalent (dually triangular) maps and finite-index subgroups of the modular group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 (cartographic groups and the modular group)

ideas.what: Explicit generator-level isomorphisms (41)-(42), including the action of complex conjugation tau_infinity on rho_infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit presentation of PGL(2,Z) as an extension of Z/2*Z/3 by an antiholomorphic involution; the S_3-symmetries of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller setting

ideas.what: Uniformization: replacing (U_{0,3}, S_3 x {1,tau}) by (Sigma^+, GL(2,Z)/±1) to read the groupoid generators as matrices.

missed.claim: Grothendieck announces generalizing the isomorphisms (40) and (43)-(44) to Pi_{0,n} and variants associated with regular n-gons. The next page suggests interpreting the analogues as remarkable discrete subgroups of GL(2,R), presumably Hecke-type triangle groups. On this page it is only announced.
missed.quote: Je vais revenir sur ces isomorphismes (40) dans un contexte un peu plus général, ci-dessous.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a groupoid- and cartographic-group-level uniformization of the S_n-symmetric Teichmüller tower by triangle and Hecke groups. It would only be of interest if the later pages actually develop it; on this page it is just a programme statement.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the classical identification of the orbifold fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,infinity} mod S_3 (with or without complex conjugation) with PSL(2,Z) / PGL(2,Z), plus the corresponding map-theoretic statements. The explicit generator formulas are careful but routine. The only potentially new thread, generalization to n-gons and Hecke groups, is merely announced here.
transcription_corrections: 'sont définis de façon standard': a small '§4' (or 'Σ4') is written under 'défi-', likely a cross-reference to section 4.
First line: 'dont le deuxième est donné par' is fine; the margin under (41) reads 'Attention : l'exposant !' (the '?' can be dropped).

The marginal NB is written obliquely in the left margin: 'NB on utilise rho_1^2 = rho_infinity^3 = 1 et tau_infinity(rho_infinity) = rho_0 rho_1 = rho_1^{-1} rho_infinity^{-1} rho_1 = rho_1 rho_infinity^{-1} rho_1'.
'car rho_infinity^3 = 1 dans pi_{0,3}^tau/<...>' — the superscript is tau, as transcribed.
The group in '(cf. aussi les générateurs de pi_{0,3}^tau ≃ ...)' looks like '\widehat{\Gamma}_{2+}' or 'Γ_2^±'; uncertain.
